{{short description|Canadian mathematician}}
'''Christiane Rousseau''' {{post-nominals|country=CAN|OC|OQ|size=100%}} (born March 30, 1954, in [[Versailles (city)|Versailles]], [[France]]) is a French and Canadian mathematician, a professor in the department of mathematics and statistics at the [[Université de Montréal]]. She was president of the [[Canadian Mathematical Society]] from 2002 to 2004.<ref name="cv">[http://www.dms.umontreal.ca/~rousseac/CV_English.pdf Curriculum vitae], retrieved 2014-12-17.</ref>

==Education and career==
Rousseau earned her Ph.D. from the Université de Montréal in 1977, under the supervision of Dana Schlomiuk, with a thesis entitled "Topos Theory and Complex Analysis".<ref name="cv"/><ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=67955}}</ref> After postdoctoral research at [[McGill University]], she joined the Montréal faculty in 1979, and was promoted to full professor in 1991.<ref name="cv"/> She was interim Director of [[Centre de Recherches Mathématiques]]  from 2008 to 2009.

She was the first female vice-president of the [[International Mathematical Union]], from 2011 to 2014. She implemented and led the Mathematics on Planet Earth initiative in 2013 (MPE 2013), supported by UNESCO, and played a leading role in having March 14 declared the International Day of Mathematics by UNESCO.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The International Day of Mathematics - Because the World Needs Math! |url=https://en.ccunesco.ca/blog/2020/3/the-international-day-of-mathematics-because-the-world-needs-math |access-date=2023-11-09 |website=Canadian Commission for UNESCO |language=en}}</ref>

== Scientific work ==
Rousseau's main areas of research are [[Differential equation|differential equations]] and [[Dynamical system|dynamical systems]]. This includes work on singularities of [[Differential equation|differential equations]], [[bifurcation theory]], [[Hilbert's sixteenth problem]] (the part about differential equations)<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Rousseau |first1=Christiane |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=_kbgNw7q2osC&pg=PA496 |title=Normal Forms, Bifurcations and Finiteness Problems in Differential Equations |last2=Sabidussi |first2=Gert |date=2004-02-29 |publisher=Springer Science & Business Media |isbn=978-1-4020-1929-6 |language=en}}</ref> as well as analysis of important differential equations in [[Mathematical Biology|mathematical biology]] such as the [[Lotka–Volterra equations|predator-prey Lotka–Volterra equations]]. Other scientific interests include applications of [[Lie algebra]] to the [[Grand Unified Theory]].  

She actively participates in mathematics popularization programs in high schools and [[CEGEP|cégeps]], namely through presentations as well as the publication of over 35 vulgarization articles in the ''Accromath'' journal.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rousseau |first=Christiane |title=Author's description |url=https://archive.wikiwix.com/cache/index2.php?url=http%3A%2F%2Faccromath.uqam.ca%2Fauthor%2Fchristiane%2F#federation=archive.wikiwix.com&tab=url |website=Accromath}}</ref>

==Recognition==
She has received the Adrien-Pouliot Prize and the Abel-Gauthier Prize of the Mathematical Association of Québec,<ref name="cv"/> and the 2009 Graham Wright Award for Distinguished Service from the Canadian Mathematical Society.<ref>[https://cms.math.ca/MediaReleases/2009/gwads-rousseau Christiane Rousseau to Receive the 2009 Graham Wright Award for Distinguished Service], [[Canadian Mathematical Society]], retrieved 2014-12-17.</ref> She also received the 2014 [[George Pólya Award]] of the [[Mathematical Association of America]] for her article about a discovery by [[Inge Lehmann]], "How Inge Lehmann Discovered the Inner Core of the Earth".<ref>[http://www.maa.org/programs/maa-awards/writing-awards/how-inge-lehmann-discovered-the-inner-core-of-the-earth How Inge Lehmann Discovered the Inner Core of the Earth], [[Mathematical Association of America]], retrieved 2014-12-17.</ref> In 2012, she became a [[fellow]] of the [[American Mathematical Society]] (AMS).<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2014-12-17.</ref> In 2017 she became the inaugural recipient of the AMS' [[Bertrand Russell]] prize for furthering human values and the common good through mathematics.<ref>{{citation|title=2018 Bertrand Russell Prize|journal=[[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]]|volume=65|issue=4|date=April 2018|page=470|url=https://www.ams.org/journals/notices/201804/rnoti-p470.pdf}}</ref>
In 2018 the [[Canadian Mathematical Society]] listed her in their inaugural class of fellows.<ref>{{citation|url=https://cms.math.ca/MediaReleases/2018/Fellows|title=Canadian Mathematical Society Inaugural Class of Fellows|publisher=Canadian Mathematical Society|date=December 7, 2018}}</ref>

In 2024, she was appointed as an officer to the [[Order of Canada]]. She lives in [[Mont-Saint-Grégoire, Quebec]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gg.ca/en/appointments-order-canada-december-2024|title=Appointments to the Order of Canada – December 18, 2024 |work=The Governor General of Canada |date=16 December 2024 }}</ref>
